text: For confirmation of minutes in the last meeting, dated 25th of June, 2020, can I please have a mover? Councillor Aiken, thank you. Seconded by Councillor Murnane. This evening, the matter for consideration is item PP1371-2019 for Taylor's Court, Highton. We received 26 objections for this application. No submitters wish to appear before us this evening, so we will not be hearing from the applicant in response either.

speaker: lewismuston
text: Councillor Muston, thank you, Chair. So, for Taylor Court, it's situated to the northern side of Taylor Court. It's an irregular lot and it has a total, irregularly shaped lot, I should say, and it has a total area of just under 2,300 square metres. The site's frontage to Taylor Court is approximately 12.2 metres. That's within its southwestern corner. The site is provided with vehicular access via an existing double crossover from Taylor Court within that southwestern corner, and it's noted that that double crossover also provides access to the neighbouring dwelling at number five, Taylor Court, as well. There are two existing drainage easements to the western side of the site. These easements run parallel to the western site boundary from the site's Taylor Court frontage to its rear boundary at the northern side. The surrounding area is an established residential area of Highton. The site is situated a minimum of 60 metres to the local shops and services within Highton Village, and it's also, it's approximately 150 metres to the core of the Highton Village. Highton Village itself being identified as a neighbourhood centre under the city's retail activity centre hierarchy. Nearby services include a mixture of primary schools, high schools, public open space, obviously the shops and services within Highton Village, and also, there's also access to bus routes along Roslyn Road, which provide connectivity to the wider municipality as well. In terms of planning controls, Fort Taylor Court is situated within the residential growth zone, and that's at that schedule two to the residential growth zone. The western side of the site is subject to a special building overlay, and the land to the immediate north and further east of the site is zone general residential zone, schedule two, and is also within a design and development overlay, schedule 14. At the western end of Taylor Court, approximately 60 metres from the subject site is the commercial one zone, which forms that Highton Neighbourhood Centre. In terms of the proposal, this application seeks a planning permit for the construction of nine dwellings and a nine lot subdivision. Proposal consists of the construction of three two-storey and six three-storey dwellings. It is proposed to subdivide the site into nine lots corresponding to the proposed dwellings. The existing vehicle crossover would be retained and upgraded, and a proposed common property access way running parallel to the western side boundary would serve each of the dwellings. The proposed dwellings would be orientated in an east-west layout in a terrace form, set back a minimum of 7.15 metres from Taylor Court, and there is also no front fencing proposed. Adjacent to the access way, the common property access way along the western side of the site would be a proposed landscaped area, which would measure six metres in width, and that landscaped area would continue from the street frontage all the way through to the site's rear boundary. Proposed development would provide a contemporary design response and incorporate cuboid built forms and with a combination of flat and shallow pitched roofs. It would also incorporate external facing materials evident in the surrounding area, such as rendered surfaces and weatherboard cladding. There are no walls on boundaries proposed, and the proposal does not include any reduction in car parking for either private or visitor car parking spaces. In fact, expanding on that, the development actually exceeds the onsite car parking requirements contained within the planning scheme. In terms of referrals, the application has been referred to internal council units and to relevant external utility servicing authorities. No objection to the grant of a permit has been received from internal council departments, and no objection to the grant of a permit has been received from external servicing authorities either. The public has been notified of the application through letters sent to adjoining owners and occupiers, and a notification sign at the site's frontage within Taylor Court. 28 letters were received objecting to the application. However, it is noted that some of these were duplicate or follow-up letters as well. The matters raised within those objections relate to neighbourhood character, dwelling density, overloading of existing services, including stormwater, electricity, gas, and sewer, negative impacts on residential amenity of neighbouring dwellings, increased traffic congestion and car parking demand, flooding, loss of biodiversity value, proposed fencing detail, construction management, and devaluation of property. There was no consultation meeting held, obviously due to the number of objections received and the inability for groups of people to meet during the coronavirus pandemic. The applicant instead provided a written response, which was circulated to submitters. On the back of that written response, there were no objections withdrawn. So the application's been assessed against the relevant planning policy, zone overlay, and particular and general provisions within the Greater Geelong Planning Scheme. The proximity of Taylor Court to the Neighbourhood Centre supports a higher density of development within the street than what has occurred to date. It's a well-serviced street and in close proximity to retail, education, recreation areas, and has decent access to public transport. The proposed development accords with the specific objectives of the scheme in this regard by proposing a residential development that increases the density and the diversity of housing on a large site close to the activity centre of Huyton. The proposed building height, bulk form, and external materials are considered to provide an appropriate design response based on the relevant policy considerations and the evidently evolving character of the surrounding locality, which is designated as an increased housing diversity area. The proposal is consistent with the intent expressed in relevant planning policy to support the evolution towards more intensive development with visually interesting built forms. The design response also accords with the purpose of the zoning of the site in this regard, being the residential growth zone in order to provide dwellings at increased densities and diversity. As the applicant has appealed to VCAT for review of the failure to determine the application within the prescribed timeframes, it's recommended that the council advocate to VCAT that it grant a planning permit for the construction of nine dwellings and nine lot subdivision at the subject site, subject to the conditions as contained within the officer report. Thank you, Chair.
